title: Transformation
idea: Brief #27. Swipe of the eye-bag device ad (232 days live) in the silent selfie + one-caption format (also backed by Jared's Oct 22 organic picks). The result comes right after the before (big promise up front), then stacked proof for a level 4-5 buyer: esthetician authority, social proof, old remedy, one-line mechanism, then our scaling offer.

script.visual: Initial image (all 3 hooks): model the reference's first frame. Woman about 50 leaning toward the mirror/phone, head tilted forward, eyes looking down and off to the side (same direction as the reference), NOT at the camera. No glowing glasses: face clear in soft natural window/bathroom light. Slowly rolling the Haven & Spool roll-on under one eye, oil sheen visible.
script.on_screen_text:
H1: the only reason my under-eyes look like I sleep 10 hours a night
H2: my esthetician told me to stop buying eye creams and use this instead
H3: women have used this on their eye bags for centuries and nobody told me

script.visual: Before: same woman, three-quarter angle looking off to the side (like the reference's 2nd clip), no makeup, flat morning light: puffy under-eye bags, crepey fine lines and crow's feet clearly visible.
script.on_screen_text: these were my eye bags before 😩

script.visual: After (the promise, right away): bed selfie in soft morning light, smiling, touching under her eye with one finger (like the reference's '18 days later'). Different day and light from the before.
script.on_screen_text: and this is me 3 weeks later 🥰 (tiny: Individual results vary)

script.visual: Authority: her lying back on a facial bed at a spa while an esthetician (hands only / out of focus) works on her face, OR her at her bathroom mirror pointing under her eye.
script.on_screen_text: my esthetician said eye creams just sit on top… she told me to roll THIS on every night 👀

script.visual: Social proof: her thumb scrolling her phone feed, short clips of different women rolling a castor oil roller under their eyes.
script.on_screen_text: then I saw it all over my feed, 43,000+ women swear by it ⭐ 4.9

script.visual: Old remedy: quick insert of castor beans and castor leaves next to the amber bottle on a bathroom shelf.
script.on_screen_text: turns out women have used castor oil under their eyes for centuries 🌿

script.visual: Mechanism: macro of the rose quartz ball gliding under her eye, oil soaking in.
script.on_screen_text: cold-pressed castor oil soaks in + holds moisture all night 💧 the cool rose quartz roller de-puffs while you apply

script.visual: Walking outside, wind in her hair, happy selfie (like the reference's last clip).
script.on_screen_text: now everyone asks if I got work done ✨

script.visual: Her hand holding the bottle up next to her face, then 2 bottles on the counter.
script.on_screen_text: Buy 1 Get 1 Free right now · $29 a bottle · 30 nights or it's free · link below

editing_notes: Replicate the reference: silent selfie clips, one caption per clip, 20-30 s, cuts every 2-3 s. Small white TikTok-style captions top-centre with 1 emoji. Shot like a real phone (front camera, natural light, slight handheld shake) so it passes as real UGC. Under-eyes only: puffy bags + crepey fine lines + crow's feet. Roller glides slowly RIGHT ON the under-eye with a visible oil sheen, never beside it, never fast dabs; use the 50ml reference in the Products tab for bottle size. Same person in every clip. The after clip (#2) is a different day and light, not a side-by-side; add small "Individual results vary" on it. Claims: how it looks only ("smoother", "less puffy"), never "gone". Doc: Brief H+S, tab #27.
Voiceover: N/A. Silent with captions only, exactly like the reference.

Avatar: One real-looking woman, about 50, natural, no glam, real skin texture and pores (no smooth AI skin). Same woman in every clip, same face, same hair. Puffy under-eye bags + crepey fine lines + crow's feet; has tried eye creams. Level 4-5 sophistication.
